details.note: Routes by path: / to the web service and /api to the booking service. The TLS certificate lives here.
A stable name and address in front of the booking pods, which come and go behind it.
One replica of the booking deployment. The deployment keeps two running, and an autoscaler adds more when CPU climbs.
Runs as a stateful set, so it keeps its name and its volume when it's rescheduled.
Outlives the pod. Snapshot it nightly and test a restore.
A config map: the database host and feature switches, read by every booking pod.
A secret, mounted into the database pod and every booking pod. Keep it out of the image and out of version control.
Scrapes every pod's metrics endpoint; alert on restarts and on pods stuck pending.
Schedules pods onto nodes, replaces any that fail and rolls out changes a pod at a time. Let a deploy pipeline apply the manifests from version control; nobody changes the cluster by hand.

name: Kubernetes deployment
note: Follow a request from the rider's phone through the ingress to a service and on to one of its pods; everything in the box runs inside the cluster. Swap the bike-hire services for yours, and keep config, secrets and storage as separate objects so any pod can be replaced.
title: Bike hire on Kubernetes
